fieldMarks: Adult drake is entirely black except for an orange knob on the bill.
Hens and young drakes are dark with a contrasting pale face and foreneck.
Crow-sized sea duck; floats buoyantly with the tail often cocked up.
behavior: More vocal than other scoters; in spring gives a musical whistled cour-loo.
Dives for mussels and other bivalves, crustaceans and marine worms at sea; eats aquatic insects, fish eggs and plants on summer fresh water.
Migrates early in spring and late in fall; coastal flocks fly low offshore.
habitat: Breeds on coastal and wet tundra and tundra openings in northern forest. Winters on bays and exposed coasts over shallow water, mostly within a mile of shore; uses the Great Lakes in migration.
range: Breeds in Alaska and northern Canada; winters along the Atlantic and Pacific coasts and occurs on the Great Lakes in migration.

lookalikes.name: Ruddy duck
lookalikes.howToTell: A winter drake ruddy duck is smaller and paler with a relatively larger bill.

aliases: common scoter (former name, now used for the Old World species)
